name: get_caller_identity
description: Return the simulated AWS account, ARN and user id (STS GetCallerIdentity).

name: list_buckets
description:
List the S3 buckets in the synthetic AWS account, one page at a time.

        Same paging as ``ListBuckets``: names in lexicographic order, ``max_buckets``
        up to 10000, and a ``ContinuationToken`` to pass back for the next page.

prefix.title: Prefix
prefix.description: Return only names starting with this string.

continuation_token.title: Continuation Token
continuation_token.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's NextContinuationToken; omit for the first page.

name: list_objects
description:
List objects in an S3 bucket (ListObjectsV2), one page at a time.

        ``max_keys`` is capped at 1000 like S3's own page size, and a rolled-up
        ``CommonPrefixes`` entry counts against it exactly as a key does. When the
        listing is truncated the reply carries ``NextContinuationToken``; pass it
        back as ``continuation_token`` for the next page. ``delimiter`` (usually
        ``"/"``) rolls keys up into ``CommonPrefixes`` instead of listing them.

prefix.title: Prefix
prefix.description: Return only names starting with this string.

max_keys.title: Max Keys
max_keys.description: Maximum object keys in one page (S3: 1-1000, default 1000).

continuation_token.title: Continuation Token
continuation_token.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's NextContinuationToken; omit for the first page.

delimiter.title: Delimiter
delimiter.description: Character that groups keys into common prefixes, usually '/' for folder-style listing.

name: get_object
description:
Read an S3 object's body: ``max_bytes`` of it from byte ``offset``, as a ``Range`` GET would.

        A text body is returned as text; a compressed or binary one is base64 in
        ``Body`` with ``BodyEncoding`` saying so, because decoding gzip or JPEG bytes
        as UTF-8 with replacement characters hands the caller a body that is neither
        the object's bytes nor readable text.

key.title: Key
key.description: S3 object key (its full path within the bucket).

max_bytes.title: Max Bytes
max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes of object content to return, so a large object cannot flood the answer.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Byte offset to start reading the object from, to page through a body larger than max_bytes.

name: storage_summary
description: Objects, bytes, versions and delete markers per bucket, and bytes per storage class.

name: list_datasets
description: List the lake's datasets: location, format, rows, partitions and classification.

name: describe_dataset
description: Full catalog entry for a dataset: column schema, classifications, partitions, owner.

name: preview_dataset

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum items to evaluate or return in one page.

name: query_datasets

Run read-only SQL (DuckDB) over the lake's datasets, each registered under its own name.

        datasets work; writes and multi-statement input are rejected.

sql.title: Sql
sql.description: One read-only SQL (DuckDB) statement over the lake's datasets, each registered under its own name.

name: read_parquet_metadata

key.title: Key

name: read_media_metadata

key.title: Key

name: list_iam_users
description:
List the account's IAM users with their access keys and MFA state.

        Each user carries the keys ``ListAccessKeys`` reports for them, with the age in
        days and the last-use facts ``GetAccessKeyLastUsed`` answers, so an access review
        does not have to walk one call per user. ``only_with_active_keys`` keeps users
        holding at least one ``Active`` key and ``key_older_than_days`` those whose oldest
        active key is older than that many days — the rotation question, computed against
        the same snapshot clock the ``CreateDate`` values are on.

        Pages like ``ListUsers``: ``max_items`` is 1-1000, ``Marker`` when truncated.

max_items.title: Max Items
max_items.description: Maximum items in one page (IAM: 1-1000, default 100).

path_prefix.description: Return only IAM entities whose path starts with this string, e.g. /service-role/.

only_with_active_keys.description: Report only users that hold an active access key.

key_older_than_days.title: Key Older Than Days
key_older_than_days.description: Report only access keys older than this many days.

name: list_iam_groups
description:
List the account's IAM groups with their policies and their members.

        The official IAM MCP server's group tools are ``list_groups``, ``get_group`` and
        ``add_user_to_group``, and the first question an agent asks of an account is what
        the job functions are and who is in them. Membership here is the same fact
        ``GetGroup`` and ``ListGroupsForUser`` answer with, and the policies include the
        inline ones no attached-policy listing shows.

path_prefix.title: Path Prefix
path_prefix.description: Return only IAM entities whose path starts with this string, e.g. /service-role/.

name: simulate_principal_policy
description:
Whether an identity may perform actions, answered from its policies.

        The official IAM MCP server publishes ``simulate_principal_policy`` as a tool of
        its own, because the review question — "can this user still delete production
        buckets?" — must be answerable without making the call: making it is either a
        denial in the audit log or a deleted bucket. The verdict is the same evaluator
        the request path uses, and ``MatchedPolicies`` names the policy responsible,
        which is what a reviewer has to change.

policy_source_arn.title: Policy Source Arn
policy_source_arn.description: ARN of the user, group or role whose effective permissions to simulate.

action_names.title: Action Names
action_names.description: API actions to simulate, e.g. s3:GetObject.

resource_arns.title: Resource Arns
resource_arns.description: ARNs of the resources to evaluate.

name: get_credential_report
description:
The account's IAM credential report, parsed into rows.

        This is the access review in one call: AWS's own guidance is to read the
        credential report to find users without MFA, passwords and keys that have not
        been rotated, and credentials still active for people who have left. The CSV
        ``GetCredentialReport`` hands back is parsed here so an agent does not have to,
        and generated on demand as ``GenerateCredentialReport`` would — the columns are
        IAM's own, sentinels (``N/A``, ``no_information``, ``not_supported``) included.

name: get_tagged_resources
description:
The estate by tag, across services, the way ``GetResources`` answers it.

        The one inventory question an agent asks that no per-service Describe answers:
        what carries a given tag, and what is missing the keys the account's own
        convention requires. ``untagged_only`` returns just the non-compliant tail, which
        is what a tag clean-up works from.

        ``GetResources`` itself is regional, so an agent asking it about a whole account
        has to call every region; ``region`` scopes this to one of them and leaving it
        empty answers for the account.

tag_values.title: Tag Values
tag_values.description: Tag values to match; empty matches any value for the key.

resource_type_filters.title: Resource Type Filters
resource_type_filters.description: Limit the answer to these resource types, e.g. ec2:instance.

untagged_only.title: Untagged Only
untagged_only.description: Report only resources carrying no tags.

region.description: AWS region to query, e.g. us-east-1; every resource call is regional.

region.title: Region

        everything the group holds, because a group whose writer went quiet a month ago
        is exactly the one being investigated.

filter_pattern.title: Filter Pattern

name: call_aws
description:
Run an AWS CLI command (``aws ec2 describe-instances --max-items 2``) against the simulator.

        Mirrors the awslabs ``aws-api-mcp-server`` entry point. The command is read with
        botocore's model of the service, serialized into the request the CLI itself
        would send, and dispatched to the same handler REST serves it with — so what
        works over REST works here, and what REST refuses is refused with REST's own
        error code and message rather than a fabricated answer. Reads are served on a
        read-only deployment, so the tool is marked read-only for the shared guard and
        enforces the posture per operation itself: a write is refused with AWS's
        ``AccessDenied``, the same refusal REST gives it.

cli_command.title: Cli Command
cli_command.description: A full AWS CLI command to run, e.g. aws s3api list-buckets.

name: suggest_aws_commands
description:
Suggest the CLI commands the simulator serves that are most relevant to a natural-language query.

        Only commands that share a word with the question are suggested, and a command
        that changes or destroys something is offered only when the question asks for
        it: ranking by word overlap alone put ``delete-object`` and ``delete-snapshot``
        at the top of "which buckets do I have?", which is a suggestion an agent acts on.

query.title: Query
query.description: Plain-English question to suggest AWS CLI commands for.
